statement.headline:
Our team invented Direct Conversion.
For over 30 years, direct conversion sensors have set new standards
for precision and image accuracy in X-ray imaging.
statement.body: By eliminating the scintillator and converting X-rays directly into electrical pulses, Athlos sensors and linear arrays eliminate the root cause of image degradation. The result is sharper detail, truer contrast, and reliable performance across the full dose range.

invented.label: Direct conversion founded by our team

tech.headline:
Direct conversion.
No intermediate steps.
No compromise.
tech.body1: Conventional X-ray sensors rely on a scintillator to first convert X-rays into visible light, which then enters a photodiode with limited fill factor and converts to electrical pulses. This indirect conversion — from X-rays to light, then from light to electrical signal — introduces significant blur, signal loss (fill factor well below 100%) and undetected X-rays due to the limited DQE of scintillators.
tech.body2: Athlos sensors use CdTe-CMOS and Si-CMOS direct conversion hybrids that convert X-ray photons directly into electric pulses that retain point accuracy. With no scintillator or phosphor layer, direct conversion avoids light spread and helps preserve spatial accuracy, contrast, and detail.

comparison.heading: Direct vs. Indirect Conversion
comparison.subheading: Direct conversion removes the scintillator light-spread stage, creating a shorter and more localized X-ray-to-signal pathway.
comparison.bottomLine: Fewer conversion stages. More direct signal localization.
comparison.ariaDescription: Side-by-side comparison of two X-ray detector types. In indirect conversion, X-rays first strike a scintillator that converts them into visible light; that light spreads laterally before reaching the photodiode and readout, softening signal localization. In direct conversion, X-rays are converted straight into electric charge inside a CdTe or silicon layer, producing tight vertical charge columns that travel directly to the CMOS readout — a shorter, more localized signal path and a sharper output.

experience.summary: Fewer conversion stages. More localized signal path.
experience.aria: Animated sequence following a single X-ray photon into two detectors. In the indirect detector, the photon strikes a scintillator that converts it into warm visible light, which spreads laterally before reaching the photodiode — a softer, wider signal. In the Athlos direct-conversion detector, the photon's energy becomes a tight, localized charge in the CdTe or silicon layer that travels straight down into the CMOS readout — a sharper, more localized signal. The final comparison shows the same test pattern softer on the indirect side and sharper on the direct side.
